full_judgment:
7. Mr. Moazzem Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney General urged that successive application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is barred by section 369 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further contended that successive application cannot be allowed on the ground of public policy. He submitted that if an application is once rejected by the High Court and another application is filed and the High Court comes to a different conclusion in the second application and allows it, then there will be contradictory and inconsistent order of the High Court. In support of his contention Mr. Moazzem Hossain has cited the case of Kishori Lal V. The Crown ILR 1945 Lahore 573, Malhari Ramaji Chikate V. Emperor, in 49 Cr. L.J. 460, Re T. Venkateswara Rao and others in AN (38) 1951 Madras 611, Brajakishor Pattanik and other V. Indian Union, in AIR 1950 Orissa 146, Mt. Haydari Begum V. Jawad Ali Shah in AIR 1934 Allahabad 22. 

 17. Our High Court has framed Rules under section 491, sub-section (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Rules 28 to 40 occurring part 2, Chapter 11 of the High Court Rules pages 156-157 to govern proceedings under section 491 of the Code. None of these Rules contain any provision barring successive application. There is no general rule of this Court either to that effect. There is, therefore, no express prohibition either in the Code or Rules, of the Court against the making of successive application on identical or fresh grounds. The Allahabad High Court in the case of Mt. Haydari Begum Vs. Jawad Ali Shah reported in AIR 1934 Allahabad 22 applying Rule 8 of the Rules of that Code which has been quo-ted above disallowed successive applications. Like the Allahabad High Court there is no Rule in our High Court Rules akin to Rule 8 of the Allahabad High Court. The case of Barajakishor Pattanik and others Vs. Indian Union of the Orissa High Court (AIR 1950 Orissa 146) cited by Mr. Moazzam Hossain does not support his contention. On the other hand, this case shows that second application on fresh ground as in the present case is maintainable. In this case, the Orissa High Court refused to consider the second application on the ground that there were no fresh grounds on which the second application challenging the detention was filed.
